Do you have experience with technical or project procurement in a larger international company? Would you like to help develop a global supply chain in an international project-driven organization? Then you may be the Purchaser we are looking for.

We are upgrading, servicing, and operating engine- and biomass-based power plants around the world. This creates a continuous need to source goods and services from subcontractors and ensure reliable transport for our customers.

For our Global Supply Chain department, we are looking for an outgoing and internationally minded colleague with commitment, determination, and a positive attitude. The department consists of 20 employees responsible for procurement, warehousing, and transport of goods and services.

BWSC – Ever better energy! 

Join us in our mission of building a world of sustainable energy and make a meaningful impact on the world of power generation and energy conversion.

BWSC is a leading player in the power generation industry, specializing in the service, operations, and maintenance of power plants. We are seeking to always provide Ever Better Energy whether it comes to optimizing a conventional power plant, operating a biomass power plant or constructing new energy facilities. Our commitment to excellence, innovation, and environmental stewardship sets us apart in the industry.

Your responsibilities

• Support Project Procurement Managers with procurement tasks related to the execution of upgrading, service- and maintenance projects for engine and biomass power plants globally.
• Obtain quotations from suppliers and place purchase orders within a defined area of responsibility.
• Participate in broader departmental activities such as category management, supplier relationship development, negotiations, and implementation of supplier agreements.
• Contribute to identifying and evaluating potential suppliers.
• Convert purchase requisitions into purchase orders.
• Maintain and update various data, including supplier data, in the ERP system.
• Follow up on purchase orders, deliveries and invoice approvals.
• Assist with various development-oriented Global Supply Chain tasks within BWSC, including work instructions and new workflows.
The work is carried out in close collaboration with other departments in a dynamic and project-oriented organization. A flexible, cooperative, and positive attitude is therefore essential.

Desired Background and Qualifications

• Experience within procurement, including purchase order placement and follow-up.
• Completed education as an office assistant and/or relevant higher education qualification.
• Minimum 3 years of practical experience with technical or project procurement.
• Strong written and spoken English skills.
• Good IT skills and experience with ERP systems, preferably Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.
• Ability to work in a structured manner and meet deadlines.
What do we offer? 

At BWSC we build inspiring careers locally and internationally and give you access to a great network of possibilities. 

We offer you a position with great colleagues and the opportunity to bring your skills into play and grow professionally and personally. As a Purchaser at BWSC, you will receive a competitive starting salary and a strong reward package.

We offer an exciting position in a skilled, collaborative, and project-driven work environment, with opportunities for professional development and growth.

We have a good canteen, fitness facilities, and an active Staff Club that organizes various events and activities. Our HQ is located in Allerød, close to the train station and only a 30-minute ride from central Copenhagen.

Ready for a challenge?  

We review applications and invite relevant candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Supply Chain Manager Anders S. A. Pedersen at asap@bwsc.dk.

BWSC is committed to promoting equality and diversity. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of ethnic background, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or age. Therefore, we do not recommend specifying age, etc., in the application. 

BWSC no longer receives or handles applications received via email due to GDPR requirements. In order for your application to be processed, you must submit your application via our online recruitment system. 

Get to know us even better on our website, www.bwsc.com, where you can learn more about our business, organization, project portfolio, and what we want to achieve at BWSC. 

About BWSC 

Burmeister & Wain Scandinavian Contractor A/S (BWSC) is a global power plant Operation & Maintenance and technical service provider with engineering expertise, enabling power plant owners to deliver cleaner and affordable energy. We are experts in servicing, upgrading, operating, and maintaining energy systems for diesel, natural gas, and renewable baseload power plants worldwide. We help our customers increase reliability and availability of energy production, improve efficiency and performance of their power plant, design and integrate future-proof technologies, and secure lower cost of maintenance.

Our people are at the core of everything we do and key to building strong relationships with our customers. We invest in our people and their wellbeing, supporting professional development and creating an environment where collaboration, knowledge sharing, and personal growth drive our continued success and growth as a company.

Are you passionate about end-to-end Supply Chain? Do you want to take Global Product Launch to the next level, coordinating with stakeholders throughout the entire value chain? Do you have an optimization mindset and can effectively manage multiple projects?

Then this might be your defining moment. Ambu is currently looking for a Global Product Launch Manager to be based at HQ in Ballerup to join our growing Global Supply Chain team!

**A role with global impact

**In the role, you will both support and take lead on assigned NPI Projects during all project phases, incorporating Global Supply Chain resources, whilst managing all critical aspect of taking new products to the market.

You will oversee execution across regions and markets, support risk‑buy management, and collaborate closely with global production sites on ramp‑up activities, capacity planning, and overall launch readiness.

Working closely with stakeholders across the entire value chain- including Global Product Management, R&D, Procurement, Production, Quality, and Commercial teams - you will act as the Supply Chain lead who drives alignment and momentum throughout the project.

Furthermore, you will be encouraged to challenge existing processes and proactively identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

**Your Main Responsibilities Will Include

**

• New Product Introductions (NPI) – during all project phases.

• Close collaboration with stakeholders globally within Ambu, as well as external suppliers.

• Support Development of the NPI / Launch process across the Ambu organization.

• Reporting to GSC Management / Relevant stakeholders.

**Suggested candidate profile

**Skills and experiences can be earned in many ways, and we understand that the best fit for the role cannot be prescribed on paper. You are however likely to succeed in this position if you have a proven track record within project management, production and risk buy handling – and can deep dive into details whilst having the overview to keep it all on track. Moreover, you’re recognized by your energetic drive, strong motivation, and accountability in everything you do.

**Furthermore, You Have

**

• Around 5 years of experience within Supply Chain and Operations Management, preferably within a production set-up.

• A Master’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, Engineering, Production or similar

• Strong, global end-to-end Supply Chain understanding across Value Chain.

• Experience in Business Intelligence.

• Strong communication skills and collaborative team-oriented mindset.

• Experience with ERP system.

• Fluency in English, both oral and written.

**About The Department

**You will join a fast-growing Global Supply Chain department, where high level of competence, humor and execution is part of everyday life. You will be reporting into the Head of Global Product Launch, Thomas Bigum. The team consists of dedicated and skilled colleagues, where you will have the opportunity for personal and professional growth. You will work from Ambu's headquarters in Ballerup, Denmark. You will, however, be working in a global context, where your stakeholders are located across the world.

**Apply for a career #ForeverForward

**The Talent Attraction team will engage with candidates on an ongoing basis; hence we encourage you to not hesitate, and apply!

If you have questions regarding the position, don’t hesitate to reach out to Head of Global Product Launch, Thomas Bigum, at tbig@ambu.com

**Ambu – a visionary and international workplace where your efforts matter

**Ambu is a company that expands rapidly and has ambitious growth targets. We meet these targets through interdisciplinary teamwork between motivated and highly skilled employees. Your contributions and efforts are crucial to our success and by joining us you will get the opportunity to work in an international head office with an informal working environment.

We offer great opportunities for personal development. Furthermore, we offer a wide range of professional, social and financial employee benefits in addition to exciting job challenges and continuous professional and personal development.

**THE OPPORTUNITY

**We are looking for a highly driven Team Manager to join Boozt Media Partnership (BMP), our in-house retail media business that helps brands grow through data-driven media solutions, creative concepts and tailored activations.

This is a player-coach role for someone who is an exceptional salesperson who knows how to drive results both individually and through a team. You will lead and develop our BMP sales team while owning your own portfolio of key clients.

Beyond hitting targets, we are looking for a strategic and commercially minded person who brings new ideas and challenges the status quo. You know how to build strong partner relationships, identify opportunities and turn them into sales and growth. Internally, you are a strong stakeholder who knows how to get people on board, drive initiatives forward and ensure our sales efforts are aligned with the wider business.

**What You Will Do

**

• Lead, coach, and challenge the sales team to deliver against ambitious targets.

• Own and grow a portfolio of key clients, building trust and acting as a strategic partner to drive larger, long-term investments.

• Drive sales performance across both your own portfolio and the wider team

• Navigate and manage internal stakeholders, collaborating cross-functionally to ensure our retail media offerings align with broader business goals.

• Identify and drive upselling and new revenue opportunities

• Use pipeline, CRM, and performance data to forecast, prioritize, and grow the business.

**YOUR PROFILE

**

• 5+ years of sales experience within media, digital advertising or a similar commercial environment

• Leadership experience or a strong track record of coaching and developing others

• A true salesperson with a strong performance and target-driven mindset

• Experience working with KPIs, CRM, pipeline management and forecasting

• Strong commercial understanding and experience with upselling

• High energy, strong communication skills and the ability to motivate others

• Fluent in English

**WHY BOOZT?

**At Boozt, you will join a fast-paced and ambitious environment where you have the freedom and responsibility to make a real impact. As Team Manager for the BMP sales team, you will have the opportunity to shape how we drive sales performance, develop our people and grow our retail media business.

You will work with passionate colleagues, leading Nordic and international brands, and a business that is constantly evolving. We value trust, ownership and the courage to challenge the status quo - and we are looking for someone who is ready to bring energy, ambition and results to the team.

**Apply today – we’re excited to learn more about you!

**_Only applications submitted in English will be considered.

_Important: Applicants must have the legal right to work in Denmark at the time of employment. Please note that this position does not include visa sponsorship or relocation support.

We review applications on an ongoing basis. You can read more about the process under **Recruitment.

****BOOZT PERKS

**

• Great personal and internal career development opportunities

• A culture built on our values of trust, freedom, and responsibility

• Driven and passionate international colleagues

• A generous employee discount

• Healthy and delicious breakfast and lunch, top-quality coffee, and fresh fruit available all day

• In-house gym, onsite masseuse, and medical doctor

• An amazing HQ in central Copenhagen – the iconic, energy-efficient Krystallen building, recognized for its architectural design and sustainability. Enjoy breathtaking city views and much more!

_Do you want to shape the inventory strategy behind one of the world's largest jewelry brands?

_At Pandora, we are on an exciting transformation journey, building smarter, more agile, and data-driven ways of working across our global retail network. We are now looking for a Specialist, Inventory Strategy to join our Global Merchandising & Supply Chain team!

In this role, you will act as the strategic link between commercial ambitions and inventory performance for one or more retail clusters. You will own inventory, challenge existing ways of working, drive data-led decisions, and ensure stock is in the right place at the right time to support growth, profitability, and an exceptional customer experience.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone in the early stages of their career or with a few years of experience under their belt, who is ready to take ownership, influence stakeholders, and grow into a strategic inventory expert within a global organization.

**What You'll Do

**As Specialist, Inventory Strategy, you will serve as the key point of coordination for inventory performance across your assigned retail clusters, partnering closely with Merchandising, Allocation, Supply Chain, Demand Planning, and regional stakeholders.

**Your Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Owning inventory performance and stock investment strategies across assigned retail clusters.

• Developing inventory frameworks that balance customer demand, commercial performance, and working capital efficiency.

• Monitoring inventory risks and proactively addressing low stock, excess inventory, and supply constraints.

• Driving inventory rebalancing strategies across the retail network to maximize stock utilization, improve availability, and support End-of-Season Sale (EOSS) objectives.

• Establishing and tracking key inventory KPIs, including stock health, forecast accuracy, sell-through, and availability.

• Supporting allocation and scarcity management decisions for high-demand or constrained products.

• Driving inventory rebalancing strategies across the retail network to maximize stock utilization and improve availability.

• Identifying opportunities to improve processes, optimize inventory flows, and increase agility across the business.

• Acting as a trusted partner to cluster stakeholders, leading discussions, challenging assumptions, and driving alignment on inventory decisions.

• Supporting strategic projects and transformation initiatives that impact the wider inventory and supply chain ecosystem.

**What We're Looking For

**We imagine you bring a combination of analytical strength, business understanding, and the confidence to engage with stakeholders across a global organization. You may come from a background in Inventory Management, Supply Chain, Allocation, Merchandise Planning, Demand Planning, or a similar analytical function.

**We Are Looking For Someone Who Has

**

• 1-4 years of relevant professional experience within Supply Chain, Inventory Planning, Allocation, Merchandise Planning, Demand Planning, or a related field.

• Experience working with retail products, inventory, or commercial planning environments.

• Strong Excel skills and experience working with large datasets.

• Experience using Power BI or similar reporting and visualization tools.

• Confidence presenting insights and leading discussions with stakeholders.

• The ability to navigate challenging conversations and influence decisions through data and commercial understanding.

• A proactive mindset and willingness to take ownership with limited supervision.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

• Curiosity and motivation to learn, grow, and continuously improve processes.

• Experience with SQL, data querying, or AI tools is considered an advantage.

**What Makes You Successful In This Role

**You are someone who is eager to step up and take ownership from day one. You thrive in a fast-paced

environment, enjoy solving complex problems, and are comfortable balancing data, business priorities, and stakeholder needs.

Most importantly, you are not afraid to challenge the status quo, drive change, and take the lead when needed.

**Additional Information

**

• Global Career Band: 5B

**Did we get your attention?

**If you see yourself in the position and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

**Icing on the cake

**You will be working out of our beautiful Head Office in Copenhagen V, established in 2016 and designed to unite and inspire our teams. Besides our beautiful interior design we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

**About Pandora

**Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

Tech-first. Ego-free. User-obsessed.

Over one million Danes use Skatteguiden to understand and optimise their taxes. We automate tax tracking, surface deductions people didn't know they had, and give users the insights they need to make better financial decisions — all directly connected to the Danish tax authority.

We're an independent company of around 50 people based in Copenhagen, with a 4.7-star App Store rating and a simple mission: make financial insight accessible to everyone, not just those who can afford an accountant.

**About The Role

**Path to Plus is the engine that converts users into paying members and keeps them there. As a Backend Engineer on this team, you'll be building and shipping features as part of a cross-functional product team with a direct commercial mission — not executing on a spec handed down to you, but helping shape what gets built and why.

This is a product engineering role. The team owns the problem, not just the delivery. That means getting involved before requirements are written, connecting your technical work to user and business outcomes, and iterating based on real feedback. You'll work closely with engineering leadership — not as a follower, but as a collaborator who contributes to the plan. If you've worked that way before — or you're actively looking to grow into it — this is the right environment.

What you'll do

• End-to-end features. Ship features as part of the team's product cycle, from problem shaping to production.

• Multi-broker architecture. Stock tax support is live. The next challenge is redesigning the current model to support multiple brokers — a real architectural problem you'll be part of solving.

• Observability. You'll help us own the health of critical business flows and catch issues before users do.

• Azure migration. We're migrating our systems in the coming months. Cloud architecture thinking will be an active part of the role.

• Tech debt on the roadmap. We believe tech debt belongs on the roadmap, not hidden under it. You'll help identify, prioritise, and plan for it alongside the team.

What we're looking for

You're a backend engineer who takes reliability and code quality seriously, and you can move fast without cutting corners. We care more about how you build and think than about which stack you've used. If most of this sounds like you, apply, even if you don't tick every box.

• Strong backend experience in production. You've built and run services that real users depend on, in Java, Kotlin, Go or a similar language. Our stack is Java and Spring Boot. If you haven't used it, we expect you to be keen to learn it quickly, and we'll help.

• Comfort with distributed systems. You've worked with message queues, relational databases, or both, and you understand the trade-offs.

• A product mindset. You care why something is built, not just how. You're happy to question a requirement, suggest a simpler path, and judge your work by its effect on users and the business.

• Good engineering habits. You can read an unfamiliar codebase, spot its strengths and weak spots, and improve it over time without needing a perfect plan first. You think about reliability and data, and you're realistic about making change in a production environment.

• Practical use of AI tools. Every engineer here uses Claude in daily work. You don't need to be an expert, but you should be curious and willing to make it part of how you work.

Bonus points

None of these are hard requirements.

• Java, Spring Boot, JUnit, RabbitMQ or MySQL specifically

• Kubernetes, Argo, GitHub Actions, Grafana or Loki

• Running services in Azure or another cloud, including tuning resources and cost

• Experience with fintech, payments, subscriptions or regulated data

Why join us

• Visible impact. You're joining a team with a full pipeline, and your work will show results quickly.

• A company serious about engineering quality. We're actively investing in elevating engineering practices across the organisation. You'll be part of that, not just a passenger.

• Solid company. Independent, profitable, growing. No VC pressure, no bloated roadmap. Just a clear mission and a team that cares.

• Good people. We take the work seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. The culture is professional, informal, and genuinely collaborative.

• Room to grow. The scope of the work and the team's ambitions mean there's real room to step up.

Practical details

Location: Copenhagen. We're an office-first company, and it's a deliberate choice. We're moving fast, we have big ambitions, and we genuinely believe that being physically together is one of the things that makes that possible. Things move quicker when you can turn your chair and talk to someone.

The office is a five-minute walk from Rådhuspladsen and stocked with everything from fruit to fizzy drinks to afternoon snacks. Lunch is at Claus Meyer's canteen just across the street — proper food, not an afterthought. If you're putting in a long day, dinner is covered too.

• Start: As soon as possible.

• Salary: Competitive and based on your experience.

• Reporting to: Engineering Manager.

Our hiring process

• Screening call with the hiring manager (30 min) — online

• Technical interview: build something together with a Backend Engineer and the Engineering Manager (60 min) — onsite

• Culture conversation with the Engineering Manager and CTO (60 min) — onsite

• Meet the CEO (30 min) — onsite

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Remote Sensing of Ecosystem Resilience across Danish Landscapes
jobs.description:
We are seeking applications for a 2 year postdoc position in the field of remote sensing of ecosystem resilience in the Section of Ecoinformatics and Biodiversity at the Department of Biology, Aarhus, University, Denmark.

Biodiversity loss, landscape management and other global change drivers might influence how vegetation reacts to extreme events such as droughts or floods. Climate change is expected to increase the frequency and intensity of extreme events, which is why it is important to monitor the resilience of vegetation to such events. Remote sensing offers the opportunity to study resistance and recovery of vegetation greenness and productivity across entire landscapes, including natural, semi-natural and agricultural vegetation.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2–year position from 1 March 2027. 
This is a fixed-term position to end on 28 February 2029.

Job description
This Postdoc position broadly aims at analyzing satellite time series to understand ecosystem responses to environmental stressors and disturbances, including extreme events like droughts and floods that might become more frequent under accelerating climate change. The main overarching research question is:

How do natural and managed ecosystems react to extreme events or disturbances, and how resilient are they?
The goal is to develop satellite-based indicators of ecosystem resilience across land-use types.

To this purpose, the Postdoc will be expected to combine multiple remote sensing techniques across scales, including Sentinel-2, Landsat or Sentinel-1. Compared to many land surface phenology studies at broad spatial scales (e.g. kilometers), the aim of this postdoc is to explore patterns at the level of individual fields, forests or grasslands in a fragmented landscape. By analysing responses across fine spatial scales, we will generate locally relevant metrics of ecosystem resilience and assess how different land-use types respond to climate anomalies.

This Postdoc position will focus on natural and agricultural landscapes, and mainly contribute to the Center for Landscape Research in Sustainable Agricultural Futures (Land-CRAFT) with the vision to provide a novel framework that tests and assesses the sustainability of agricultural production, both within Denmark and globally. The candidate will be part of the Section for Ecoinformatics and Biodiversity (ECOINF), Department of Biology.

The Postdoc will work directly with Prof. Fabian D. Schneider and collaborate with Prof. Signe Normand.
Applicants are encouraged to submit an individual, short project proposal of 1 to 2 pages maximum, showing how the applicant’s methodological competences can be used for the research and demonstrating the applicant’s understanding of related research, including referenced literature.

Your profile
We are seeking highly motivated Postdoc candidates interested in a scientific career. The applicant should hold an internal fascination for the topic, be independent, have excellent writing skills, and should be enthusiastic about working in an interdisciplinary and international academic environment.

Applicants are expected to have a PhD degree within ecology, Earth system science, geography, biology or similar, and have experience with: 

• Geospatial and statistical analyses of remote sensing and ecological data,
• Good programming skills, ideally using R, Python, or similar,
• Land cover and land use change,
• Multispectral remote sensing, and ideally multi-scale remote sensing tools,
• Biogeography, ecosystem or biodiversity science, including an understanding of the concept of ecosystem resilience and remote sensing of vegetation stress.
We expect the candidate to have strong knowledge and/or strong interest in remote sensing, sustainability and biodiversity, data science and agricultural and natural systems in Danish or European landscapes.

Important personal qualities are to be creative, good at problem-solving, a team-worker, independent, well structured, and keen to work across disciplines and societal sectors. Very good oral and written communication skills in English (fluent English) are expected.
Holding a B driver’s license is an advantage.

Who we are
The Department of Biology (http://bio.au.dk/) provides a framework for research and teaching in all major biological subdisciplines. The department is especially known for its research contribution in biodiversity, global change and conservation biology, aquatic biology and ecology, arctic environment and ecosystems, genetics and evolution, microbiology and zoophysiology. The department currently encompasses approximately 200 academic and technical staff and 45 PhD students while 400 students follow the BSc and MSc programs offered by the institute. 
The department offers a vibrant and informal research environment with a long-standing tradition of collaboration with international university partners. Much of the internal communication is in English and we welcome international applicants.

What we offer 
• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators 
• a work environment encouraging lively, open and critical discussion 
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance

Place of work and area of employment 
The place of employment is Aarhus University, Department of Biology, Section for Ecoinformatics and Biodiversity (ECOINF), Ny Munkegade 114, DK-8000 Aarhus C, Denmark, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with affiliated institutions. 
The work involves some periods of field work away from Aarhus.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Tenure Track Assistant Professor, Fabian Daniel Schneider, +4520906289, fabian.schneider@bio.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 3 November 2026. 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: Manager for the Drug Product Development and Analysis Team
jobs.description:
Do you thrive in a dynamic environment where you can explore scientific challenges and have a significant impact? Are you passionate about developing life-saving vaccines, and enjoy close collaboration and leading a small development team?

We are expanding and looking for a new Manager to support our development projects!

The Department of Environmental Science at Aarhus University, Roskilde, Denmark, invites applications for a permanent position as Associate Professor in Environmental Chemistry. We seek a motivated and collaborative researcher who will contribute to improving and expanding our internationally recognised research and research-based advisory and teaching activities within environmental chemistry and related disciplines. The position is available from April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a permanent position starting April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
The Department of Environmental Science at Aarhus University aims to expand and diversify its research, teaching, and advisory activities addressing current and future environmental challenges. We are therefore seeking an Associate Professor in Environmental Chemistry to contribute to the continued development of the Section for Environmental Chemistry and Toxicology.

The candidate is expected to establish and maintain a research profile while contributing to collaborative research activities across the department and with external partners. The position offers considerable freedom to develop new research directions within environmental chemistry and related disciplines under the responsibility to keep your group including yourself mainly externally funded.

The Associate Professor will contribute to:
 * Development of an internationally strong and externally funded research programme. 
 * Research addressing the occurrence, fate, transport, transformation, exposure, and impacts of chemical contaminants in natural and engineered systems. 
 * Research-based advisory activities for Danish ministries, public authorities, and other stakeholders. 
 * Teaching and course development at Life Long education, MSc, and PhD levels. 
 * Supervision of MSc students, PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, and other junior researchers. 
 * Development of interdisciplinary collaborations across environmental chemistry, toxicology, microbiology, biotechnology, modelling, and data science. 
 * Knowledge exchange and collaboration with governmental agencies, industry partners, and international research networks.

The selected candidate is expected to contribute directly to both basic and applied research and to support the department's longstanding tradition of combining scientific excellence with societal impact through research-based advisory services

Your profile
Applicants hold a PhD in Environmental Chemistry or a closely related discipline.

The selected candidate should have documented research experience within at least one area of environmental chemistry and demonstrate the ability to develop an internationally visible research profile.

Particular emphasis will be placed on:
 * Scientific productivity documented through publications in international peer-reviewed journals. 
 * Ability to develop and maintain national and international research collaborations. 
 * Experience in obtaining external research funding, or clear potential to do so. 
 * Experience with university teaching and supervision. 
 * Effective communication and collaboration skills. 
 * Commitment to contributing to an inclusive and collegial research environment.

In addition, experience within the following areas will be considered:
 * Development and application of analytical methods for trace analysis of organic contaminants in environmental and biological matrices.
 * High-resolution mass spectrometry, including target, suspect screening, or non-target workflows.
 * Environmental fate, transport, and transformation of organic contaminants.
 * Environmental monitoring programmes and environmental assessment.
 * Exposure assessment and chemical risk assessment.
 * Environmental data analysis, chemometrics, or environmental data science.
 * Research-based advisory activities, including experience supporting governmental authorities or regulatory agencies.
 * Experience with the Danish environmental advisory system or similar national or international regulatory frameworks.
 * Interdisciplinary research bridging environmental chemistry with toxicology, ecotoxicology, microbiology, biotechnology, engineering, or computational sciences.

Qualifications at the Associate Professor level will be assessed in accordance with the criteria specified in the Danish university job structure and Aarhus University's assessment criteria for permanent academic positions.

Who we are
The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department under the Faculty of Technical Sciences at Aarhus University. The knowledge base encompasses fields such as social science, geography, economics, and policy analysis, in addition to mathematical modeling, physics, chemistry, toxicology, and microbiology. Both pure and applied research is conducted on some of the major challenges facing society, such as pollution and pollution control mechanisms, management of land, soil, water, air and biodiversity, protection of ecosystem services and climate change. Research based advisory services within these areas are offered to ministries and other stakeholders and central to the Department economy. Currently, about 150 staff and PhD-students are working at the department. Further information may be found at http://www.envs.au.dk.

The selected candidate will be affiliated with the Section for Environmental Chemistry and Toxicology. The section conducts research and research-based advisory work targeting a better understanding of the transport and fate of organic pollutants in the environment, as well as a better understanding of the links between environmental chemistry, toxicology and human exposure. This includes tools to identify and quantify impacts, which can act as indicators of emerging problems. The aim is to provide the highest capability in Denmark for assessing risks associated with the distribution and fate of organic pollutants in the environment.

What we offer 
The department and section offer:
● An active, internationally recognised research environment
● a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories with high-end analytical equipment
● an interdisciplinary environment with both national and international collaborators as well as authorities and private companies
● a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
● a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
● a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.

Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work will be at Aarhus University, RISØ Campus, in Roskilde, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark. The city of Roskilde (www.roskilde.dk) is located close to Copenhagen. The area provides immediate access to a wealth of cultural and recreational pursuits.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Head of Section, Pedro Carvalho, +45 8715 8462, pedro.carvalho@envs.au.dk or Head of Department, Carsten Suhr Jacobsen, +45 2537 7667, csj@envs.au.dk. 

Technical Sciences Tenure Track
Aarhus University offers talented scientists from around the world attractive career perspectives via the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme. Highly qualified candidates are appointed as Assistant Professors for a period of six years with the prospect of performance- based advancement to a tenured Associate Professorship. 

The aim of the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme is to:

• attract outstanding talented individuals that are competitive at an international level
• to promote the early development of independent research success early in the career of scientists
• to create transparency in the academic career path
As part of the tenure track position, the candidate is offered:

• access to research infrastructure
• capability development, including postgraduate teacher training
• a mentoring programme
• support to develop scientific networks and to secure interdisciplinary research at the highest level
As part of the Aarhus University Tenure Track Programme, the University carries out a mid-way evaluation to review the progress of the tenure track candidate after three years, according to the same criteria used in the final tenure review. The final tenure review is conducted after five and a half years. If the review is positive, the candidate will be offered a tenured position as Associate Professor at Aarhus University.

Please refer to the tenure track guidelines for the tenure review criteria and for the tenure review process.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation. 

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in RNA function and gene regulation
jobs.description:
The laboratory of Ulf Vang Ørom is inviting applications for a 2-year postdoctoral position at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics at Aarhus University.

The position will focus on RNA and its role in regulating cellular pathways relevant for metabolic processes.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2–year position from February 1 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter with possibility for extension of the employment.

Job description
You will be working using several methods to study RNA, protein-interactions and epigenetics, often including high through-put methods. The project focuses on novel aspects linking RNA, metabolism and epigenetics, and allows for active involvement in shaping the project within its duration. You will be working with a high degree of independence and in collaboration with other researchers at the institute and internationally.

Your profile
Applicants should have a PhD degree in a relevant area and expertise with working with RNA and high through-put methods.

Applicant should have a high-quality publication record and excellent language (English) skills.

Who we are
The Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics (https://mbg.au.dk/en/) hosts researchers in the areas of RNA and protein biology, bioinformatics and nutrition, as well as plant research, giving great opportunities for interdisciplinary collaborations.

What we offer 
The department offers

• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment
• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Universitetsbyen 81, 8000 Aarhus, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments. 

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Ulf Vang Ørom, PhD, +45 22288766

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 30 November 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc Positions in Natural Language Processing (CPH)
jobs.description:
The Department of Computer Science at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for two or more postdoc positions in the area of Natural Language Processing (NLP). The positions are open for appointments from January 1, 2027 or soon thereafter. The duration of the positions is one or two years, depending on the candidate’s qualifications and preferences. The positions are at AAU’s Copenhagen campus, located at the waterfront in Sydhavnen.

The application deadline is Monday, November 9, 2026. Interviews are tentatively planned for December 10, 2026.

The positions are hosted within the Natural Language Processing (NLP) research group https://aaunlp.github.io/ at AAU Copenhagen, and postdocs will work under the academic leadership of Professor Johannes Bjerva https://bjerva.github.io/. The NLP group is a rapidly expanding research environment with strong activities in multilingual NLP, LLM security, linguistically informed approaches to NLP, factuality in LLMs, and socially sustainable AI. The group is supported by several major national and international research grants – in 2026, we have grown to 20 researchers, including a full professor, four assistant professors, one postdoc, two research assistants, and 12 PhD students.

As a postdoc, you will join a highly collaborative, international, and ambitious research community, with access to state-of-the-art computational resources. In your role, you will have the opportunity to develop an independent research profile and compete for individual fellowships and faculty positions. The positions include the opportunity to undertake one or more research stays abroad to facilitate knowledge exchange with top research environments worldwide. The positions are in part funded by a DFF: Sapere Aude project (“Building TRUST in Text: Linguistically Motivated Language Model Detection”) Building TRUST in Text: Linguistically Motivated Language Model Detection - Aalborg University's Research Portal, an NNF: Ascending Data Science Investigator project (“LM2-SEC: Linguistically Motivated Language Model Security”)  https://vbn.aau.dk/en/projects/linguistically-motivated-language-model-security/, and an Erasmus+ project on AI-based Personal Language Learning Assistants in collaboration with VSKDansk  https://www.brondby.dk/om-kommunen/nyheder/2025/08/vskdansk-far-eu-stotte-til-udvikling-af-ai-baseret-sprogtutor.

Your work tasks

As a postdoc, you will conduct research within the area of multilingual NLP. We are seeking postdocs with two distinct profiles within this area:

• Postdoc 1: Security, Safety, and Privacy in Natural Language Processing and AI, with a focus on Large Language Models (LLMs), LLM-based systems, and Agentic AI

• Postdoc 2: AI-based personal language learning assistants (1 year) and AI security (1 year).

Furthermore, there will be the possibility to gain experience as a co-supervisor for PhD students associated with these projects, and to supervise students on BSc. and MSc. levels.

The positions are embedded in an active and rapidly growing research environment, including ongoing projects on, e.g., AI security, epistemic diversity, linguistically motivated NLP, and knowledge-graph grounded factuality in LLMs. The postdocs will work both independently and collaboratively within the group and will have opportunities to engage with national and international partners. As a part of the projects funding these positions, we will host internationally recognised researchers at AAU, creating additional opportunities for collaboration and knowledge exchange.

Your competencies

We are looking for candidates motivated to make fundamental scientific contributions to multilingual NLP and AI security. Candidates should have the ambition of reaching an internationally leading level of research excellence by building their own research profile, while contributing to the research environment.

Applicants must have:

• A relevant PhD degree (e.g., NLP, AI, ML, Security, Cryptography, or a related field) and a relevant MSc degree (e.g., Computer Science, Software Engineering, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Computational Linguistics, or a related field)

• Strong skills in machine learning and deep learning

• Extensive experience with modern ML and NLP methods, including experience with experimentation, and with publishing in top-tier venues (e.g. ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS, ACL, EMNLP, TACL)

• Excellent communication skills in English

Applicants with documented experience in security, privacy, safety, or robustness will be preferred.

**Qualification requirements

**Appointment as postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

Who we are

According to the most recent US News and World Ranking, Aalborg University ranks 4th in Europe and 27th in the world within Best Universities for Engineering. According to a 2018 MIT report, Aalborg University is considered to have the 4th best engineering program in the world. According to the recent Times Higher Education Impact ranking, Aalborg University ranks 9th in the World for UN SDG Impact.

The Department of Computer Science at Aalborg University is highly regarded among researchers, students, and external partners because of our leading research, education, and collaboration. The department currently has more than 170 scientific staff, 20 administrative staff, and 1,100 students. Education and research are built around AAU's problem-based learning model.

The Section for Copenhagen at the department is a highly collaborative research environment, currently expanding from around 40 employees to approximately 60 over the next few years. The section includes members from research groups within NLP, AI, ML, Databases, Formal Methods, Human-Centred Computing, and others, and is uniquely characterised by an open, friendly, and supportive atmosphere. Daily life in the section is marked by informal interactions, knowledge sharing, and a strong sense of community. We also host a bi-weekly SemiBar (a combined seminar and Friday bar), where staff are challenged to present their research in a manner that provokes discussion across our diverse scientific backgrounds, along with regular social events, reading groups, cross-group research activities, and a newly established local PhD organisation promoting an active social and scientific life among our most junior researchers. Together, these initiatives create a dynamic and welcoming environment for early-career researchers and senior staff alike.

The Natural Language Processing (NLP) group, led by Professor Johannes Bjerva, is a rapidly expanding research environment specialising in multilingual NLP, LLM security, linguistically informed AI, and trustworthy language technologies. The group hosts several major research projects funded by, e.g., the Carlsberg Foundation, Danmarks Frie Forskningsfond (DFF), the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and AAU’s AI:X initiative. The group collaborates broadly across Europe and globally, and offers an inclusive, ambitious, and supportive research culture.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Cover letter, stating your motivations for applying and your qualifications in relation to the position – at most one page.

- Please indicate your preferred starting date, and your preferred duration of employment (at least 1 year, and at most 2 years).

- We ask applicants not to use generative AI or writing assistant tools in the preparation of their cover letter, except for basic grammatical and spelling correction.

• Curriculum Vitae (CV) - at most two pages

• A full list of publications.

- For three of these publications, include a single brief paragraph detailing your contributions to the work.

• Diplomas (bachelor, master's, and PhD degree diplomas)

• Project description – at most two pages.

• Please describe your research vision for the position in relation to the project topics outlined above.

• Other relevant document

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

**Do you have any questions?

**If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

**Salary and terms of employment

**The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Postdoc”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.
